To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of a contactless conductivity detector for enantiomeric separations in CE is feasible, (2) it is not necessary to use derivatization or visualization agents for detection, (3) it is possible to detect enantiomers of basic drugs and neutral compounds in the presence of a high background electrolyte concentration and (4) the detection limit is sufficient to detect enantiomeric impurities of drugs in the presence of the main enantiomer.
contactless conductivity detection (CCD) was successfully demonstrated for the separation of enantiomers of basic drugs and of amino acids in capillaries coated with non-charged chiral selector.
contactless conductivity detection is a very sensitive and universal detection method for the enantiomer separation in CE.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and the optimization of a new detection technique for CE.
the development of a new detection method, contactless conductivity detection (CCD), for capillary electrophoretic (CE) separation methods.

the development of new analytical methods for the separation, identification and quantification of organic compounds in complex mixtures by using capillary electrophoretic techniques and the combination of these methods with mass spectrometry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

contactless conductivity detection in CE is a powerful tool in the separation of enantiomers, and the method is applicable to the determination of enantiomeric excesses.
